title: Exact linear functors preserve the signed Koszul completion model
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be small ringed sites, and let a commutative ring $A$ act on $R,S$ by global sections. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] be additive, exact and $A$-linear: $F(a f)=aF(f)$ for every $a\in A$ and module map $f$. Suppose its canonical countable-product comparison $F(\prod_m M_m)\to\prod_m F(M_m)$, characterized by the projections, is invertible. Assume countable products are exact in both module categories. Fix $r\ge0$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in A$. For $m\ge1$ set $Q_m(R)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r[R\xrightarrow{a_i^m}R]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$, with transitions multiplication by $a_i$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor; define $Q_m(S)$ similarly. Use the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a complex $C$, set $B_R(C)=\prod_m(C\otimes_R Q_m(R))$, let $s$ be the transition shift, and define
$$H_R(C)^q=B_R(C)^q\oplus B_R(C)^{q-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy).$$
Let $\eta_C:C\to H_R(C)$ be $c\mapsto((c\otimes1)_m,0)$. Define $H_S(FC)$ and its unit by the same formulas. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$h_C:F(H_R(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(FC),\qquad h_C F(\eta_C)=\eta_{FC},$$
using the canonical finite-biproduct comparisons and countable-product comparison, with the same ordering of Koszul factors. It descends to the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Thus invertibility of $\eta_C$ in the derived category implies invertibility of $\eta_{FC}$. The empty scalar list is allowed. This is a statement about the explicit signed model, not a choice of a map between unspecified cones.
